clue.text: Plant agents to follow one to California

indicators.note: agents that follow come behind, so their letters are placed after the others

parts.note: A as the indefinite article, meaning one
CA is the postal abbreviation for California
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents

explanation.surface: Spies are told to plant themselves by trailing someone out to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the spy's verb, but it is the definition; 'to follow' puts the agents after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a tree or shrub, commonly called wattle, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Stalin was wrong to stand up during short journey

indicators.note: something cut short loses its final letter
in a down clue, standing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
one thing happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: a commute, a regular journey to work, without its last letter
a sin is a wrong, here written upwards

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a wrong committed while standing on a brief trip, oddly tied to Stalin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalin' is the definition by example; the reversed wrong goes inside the shortened commute.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin led the Soviet Union and was a member of its party, so he is an example of a communist.

clue.text: Runs into driver when bad-tempered

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone crashes into a motorist while in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby is an informal synonym for irritable, like a crab snapping at whoever comes near.

clue.text: Gave up Mark when sleeping around

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: abed means in bed, asleep
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Mark, a person, quit something while he was dozing in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is a plain noun for a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from something, so abstained matches gave up in the past tense.

clue.text: Refined translation lacks it

indicators.note: something that lacks letters has them taken out

parts.note: a subtitle is an on-screen translation of film dialogue
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a polished translation has lost something.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle means delicate and finely judged, which is close to refined or sophisticated.

clue.text: Grow up with "Dandy"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to increase in size
second meaning: an old-fashioned word for a fashionable man

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the Dandy comic, read by children who grow up, but it means a stylish man.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is both a verb for expanding and a dated noun for a smartly dressed gentleman.

clue.text: Pack cab then reverse over large bird

indicators.note: to reverse is to turn back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lying over something means covering it, so these letters wrap around

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Load up the taxi, then back it over a big bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large bird' reads as one phrase, but the size word supplies a letter and only 'bird' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackcap is a small European warbler, named for the male's dark crown.

clue.text: Inclined to have spare time

parts.note: spare as an adjective means thin, lean
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone is disposed to enjoy free time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare time' reads as leisure, but 'spare' means thin and 'time' is just its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so it means tilted or rested at an angle.

clue.text: Return flag to fighter — it keeps things on the level

definitions.text: it keeps things on the level

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a flag or flagstone is a paving slab
the MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: Hand a banner back to a warrior, who stays even-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' suggests a banner but means a flat stone; the whole of slab plus jet is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimbals are pivoted rings that hold a compass or camera horizontal however its mount tilts.

clue.text: Pull up plug and reach out for insulating material

parts.note: a tug is a pull, here written upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom
out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tap is a plug or stopper for a cask
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician tugs out a plug and stretches for some insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutta-percha is a latex from Malaysian trees, once used to insulate undersea telegraph cables.

clue.text: Issue from animal back to front

indicators.note: bringing the back to the front moves the last letter round to the start

parts.note: a manatee is a sea cow

explanation.surface: A problem arises from an animal turned the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final letter moves, not the whole word reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue, as a verb, is to flow out or come forth, which is what emanate means.

clue.text: It improves join after henna treatment

indicators.note: a treatment works something over, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: these letters rearranged
to cement is to join firmly

explanation.surface: A beauty product claims to make things better once the henna is applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the join word behind the rearranged dye.
explanation.definitionFit: An enhancement is something that makes a thing better, so it is what improves.

clue.text: Digital attachments to vessel reveal basic plan

parts.note: nails are attached to the digits, the fingers and thumbs
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Accessories fixed to a ship show a rough design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' sounds like computing, but it refers to digits, the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a brief outline, small enough to fit on a thumbnail.

clue.text: Similar to taking heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its inner letters count

parts.note: the inner letters, without the outer ones

explanation.surface: Something feels like being encouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking heart' reads as gaining courage; here the heart is that of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin to means related or comparable, as in kin, a synonym of resembling.

clue.text: Missing the start of defence evidence

indicators.note: missing the start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: vindication is a defence or justification

explanation.surface: A court case lacks the opening proof from the defence team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' must be turned into its synonym before the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication is a sign that points to something, a looser synonym of evidence.

clue.text: Lacking will to make it neatest

indicators.note: making something from materials means building them into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone without motivation won't tidy things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' suggests determination, but it is a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestate describes someone who dies without having made a valid legal testament.

clue.text: Repeating "Crucial time to replace MP"

indicators.note: replacing means one item takes another's place in the word

parts.note: imperative means essential, crucial
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written, the letters swapped out

explanation.surface: A news report repeats that it is vital to replace a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative means done again and again, each pass repeating the process.

clue.text: Repair or undo?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mend by sewing
second meaning: to ruin someone by framing or betraying them

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses look opposite; British slang uses stitch up for setting someone up to take the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitch up means to sew a tear closed and, informally, to frame or cheat a person.

clue.text: Statute: "Dye works to provide tax"

indicators.note: works, as in a factory, processes material into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A law states that dyeworks must pay a levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun for a factory, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate duty was the former British levy on a dead person's property, a death tax.

clue.text: Eastern English river bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a river flowing through Northamptonshire and the Fens to the Wash

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a waterbird found on an English river; the two are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nene is a river of eastern England, and the nene is a goose native to Hawaii.

clue.text: How to get juice from orange in church?

definitions.text: How to get juice from orange in church?

parts.words: How to get juice from orange
parts.note: surface reading: an instruction for extracting fruit juice
setter's reading: the instruction, said as a two-word phrase, names a raised stand found in church

explanation.walkthrough: Squashing fruit to a mush and the instruction to do so give the name of a church fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpit is the raised enclosed platform in a church from which the preacher speaks.

clue.text: Snack with drinks a tradition

parts.note: cocktails are mixed drinks
taken as written
usage means custom or tradition

explanation.surface: Nibbles served alongside drinks are a time-honoured custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snack with drinks' looks like the whole definition, but 'drinks' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail sausage is a small party sausage, a finger food served at drinks parties.

clue.text: Main growth in fuel outside Russian capital

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it

parts.note: coal is a fuel

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: The chief growth in the fuel industry lies beyond Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea in old poetic usage, so main growth is something growing in the sea; 'Russian capital' is not Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is built up by colonies of small marine animals, a growth in the sea.

clue.text: Mean rascal extremely lazy

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A stingy scoundrel is very idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for the rascal, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest without saying outright, which is one sense of the verb mean.

clue.text: Shows fruit to flier

parts.note: to air something is to show it, so airs means shows
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Someone displays fruit to a pilot or passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a powered lighter-than-air craft, so it flies and is a flier.

clue.text: Delegate likely to accept flower in

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it inside

parts.note: apt means likely, as in apt to happen
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is in Italy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A representative will probably let a flower come inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river, something that flows; 'Delegate' is the verb, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to assign them a role, which is what delegating a person does.

clue.text: Careless mole swallows prune

indicators.note: something that swallows another holds it inside

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
to lop is to prune, cutting branches off

explanation.surface: A clumsy mole eats a dried plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is the secret agent and 'prune' the verb, not the animal and the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy means done without care or attention, a close synonym of careless.

clue.text: Number one held both

indicators.note: something held is gripped from the outside, so it sits within

parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, and ether is an anaesthetic
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The top number kept both of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Either can mean each of two, as in trees on either side, so it covers both.
